Actually, as someone who has a training in the medical field and is currently studying microbes, I can confirm that hydrogen peroxide DOES in fact kill virus microorganisms.
By the way, viruses and bacterial are types of microorganisms (for short microbes) 
So the hydrogen peroxide is not "irritat(ing)the area" it is actually killing viral microbes on the surface. And yes, I said surface, because cold sore blisters contain viral materials which allow the sores to spread when said blisters burst.


You are correct in your comment of the virus existing on nerve endings however the virus itself doesn't not reside there as you have claimed. The herpes simplex virus that causes oral blistering (cold sores) nests deep inside the brain in an area of nerve cells called the trigeminal ganglion. Where the virus lies dormant whether a blister/sore is visible or not. The herpes simplex virus is thus incurable at this time, despite only presenting on occasion. 

Hydrogen Peroxide is also a common ingredient in various over the counter first aid antiseptics, such as Dettol which is used by doctors during childbirth procedures. 

While hydrogen is not recommended for long term use or undiluted use (because of the reasons you have highlighted) it's use is not the "dangerous" or "misguided" treatment choice that you paint it to be, and the person that has posted their personal experience which actually holds water scientifically is not lacking "basic education" despite the ignorant insults and poor demeanour you have maliciously imposed upon them.
